name: Sun-and-planet specification
summary: Watt's patented sun-and-planet gearing turned an engine's back-and-forth beam motion into continuous rotation, letting steam engines drive mills and factory machinery.
description: Watt's fifth patented method converts reciprocating engine motion into continuous shaft rotation with sun-and-planet gearing; the specification also describes an internal-tooth variant.
tier_reason: Prefer consistency with the other separately scoped patent specifications; rank the implemented rotative system separately from its legal description. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: One patent text for a gearing that worked around the crank patent, used by the engine trade for some years before being superseded.

why: Manufacturers wanted rotary power for mills, and a rival patent on the simple crank pushed Watt to patent alternative ways of producing rotation.

date.basis: Patent granted 25 October 1781; detailed specification signed 13 February and enrolled 23 February 1782.

events.statement: Watt's fifth patented method converts reciprocating engine motion into continuous shaft rotation with sun-and-planet gearing; the specification also describes an internal-tooth variant.
events.caveats: The primary specification was read in a web transcription of a scholarly documentary edition. Its OCR errors and intermediate hosting are recorded; invention priority between Watt and Murdock is not asserted.

evidence.locator: Section 23: introductory dates; Fifth Method; drawing No. 5 figures 1–4; concluding enrollment
evidence.supports: Mechanism, internal variant and distinct grant/specification dates.

evidence.locator: AdminHistory: Boulton & Watt, 1775–1800, paragraph on subsequent patents
evidence.supports: 25 October 1781 patent and its sun-and-planet content.

date.basis: The archive dates the Soho engine’s corn-mill service to 1783 and gives conflicting March/June records.

events.statement: A Soho double-acting engine used the internal sun-and-planet gearing included in Watt’s 1781 patent to drive a corn mill.
events.scope: Internal-tooth sun-and-planet gearing converting a reciprocating steam engine’s motion into shaft rotation.
events.caveats: The operating month is disputed. This shows use of the internal variant, not market availability of all five mechanisms in the specification.

evidence.locator: MS 3147/5/1340, technical description and final paragraph
evidence.supports: Describes the 18-inch double-acting rack-and-sector engine with internal sun-and-planet gear driving a corn mill; records disagree on March/June 1783.

evidence.locator: 1781 specification, fifth method and internal-tooth variant
